title: Event
description: One point in space and time, or a long process with an interval and usually no place. An event points at a place record rather than repeating its coordinates; region is derived at index time from that place, and on the record it is an optional override. Since M30a-3 it is optional everywhere: an event with neither a place nor a region is drawn in no lane and the validator warns `no-lane` rather than refusing it.

names.description: What else this event is called: the common name where the title is the formal one, the name in another language, the name a source uses. Optional, unlike an actor's or a place's, because the title is already the display name and this list exists for search — an event nobody calls anything else carries no key at all. Held to a shape by rule 18, as the other two are: no empty list, no name twice, and never the title itself. Search does not fold it yet; that is the search shard's, and plan decision 5.

place.description: The place record this event happened at, or null for a process with no honest point, which is then timeline-only and carries a region where anybody can say which lane it belongs in.

regionNote.description: Why the lane on this record is an override rather than the derivation. Written only beside a `region`, and only by whatever set it: the import writes it because a placeless event or a place whose own point reaches no polygon has to be given a lane, and a lane given by a tool is not the same fact as one derived from a coordinate (health review A, finding 23a). A person writing an override says why here too, in a sentence.

parent.description: The larger event this one is part of: a battle inside a war, a decree inside a revolution. One parent, so the events form a tree; that it resolves to an active event and that the tree has no cycle is rule 24, and a child dated outside its parent is a warning. It is a display fact and never an argument: `parent` does not enter the adjacency, so consequences, ancestors, convergence and the horizon stay edge-only (plan decision 4).

scope.description: How wide an event is, for the two cases a mark cannot show: a regional or a worldwide event is drawn as a band across the timeline and a wash over the map rather than as a point, so a world war or a pandemic reads as the ground the smaller events stand on (plan decision 4). Absent means an ordinary event. The vocabulary is EVENT_SCOPES in src/vocab.js.

category.description: What kind of thing this event is, from the closed list in data/categories.json — war, treaty, election and the rest. In data and not in code, so that adding one is an edit to that file (plan decision 13); a category outside the list is the warning `category-unknown`, not an error, until every event carries one. The map draws one glyph per category (M30b).

actors.description: The actors of this event and what each did in it — not everyone alive. A role comes from the closed list in data/roles.json; one outside it is the warning `role-unknown` until M32b applies the mapping and makes it an error. `note` is the free text beside the role — "president under whom it was held" — which is what the phrase a drafting run wrote becomes once the role itself is a vocabulary. That every actor resolves is rule 14.
